work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter, on the walls, a Master Gunner and his Boy.

lines.text: Sirrah, thou know'st how Orleans is besieged,
lines.plainText: Sirrah thou know'st how Orleans is besieged

lines.text: And how the English have the suburbs won.
lines.plainText: And how the English have the suburbs won

lines.text: Father, I know; and oft have shot at them,
lines.plainText: Father I know and oft have shot at them

lines.text: Howe'er unfortunate I miss'd my aim.
lines.plainText: Howe'er unfortunate I miss'd my aim

lines.text: But now thou shalt not. Be thou ruled by me.
lines.plainText: But now thou shalt not Be thou ruled by me

lines.text: Chief master-gunner am I of this town;
lines.plainText: Chief mastergunner am I of this town

lines.text: Something I must do to procure me grace.
lines.plainText: Something I must do to procure me grace

lines.text: The Prince's espials have informed me
lines.plainText: The Prince's espials have informed me

lines.text: How the English, in the suburbs close intrench'd,
lines.plainText: How the English in the suburbs close intrench'd

lines.text: Wont, through a secret grate of iron bars
lines.plainText: Wont through a secret grate of iron bars

lines.text: In yonder tower, to overpeer the city,
lines.plainText: In yonder tower to overpeer the city

lines.text: And thence discover how with most advantage
lines.plainText: And thence discover how with most advantage

lines.text: They may vex us with shot or with assault.
lines.plainText: They may vex us with shot or with assault

lines.text: To intercept this inconvenience,
lines.plainText: To intercept this inconvenience

lines.text: A piece of ordnance 'gainst it I have placed
lines.plainText: A piece of ordnance 'gainst it I have placed

lines.text: And even these three days have I watch'd,
lines.plainText: And even these three days have I watch'd

lines.text: If I could see them.
lines.plainText: If I could see them

lines.text: Now do thou watch, for I can stay no longer.
lines.plainText: Now do thou watch for I can stay no longer

lines.text: If thou spy'st any, run and bring me word;
lines.plainText: If thou spy'st any run and bring me word

lines.text: And thou shalt find me at the Governor's.
lines.plainText: And thou shalt find me at the Governor's

lines.text: Father, I warrant you; take you no care;
lines.plainText: Father I warrant you take you no care

lines.text: I'll never trouble you if I may spy them.
lines.plainText: I'll never trouble you if I may spy them

content.text: Enter, on the turrets, Salisbury and Talbot, Sir William Glansdale, Sir Thomas Gargrave and others.

lines.text: Talbot, my life, my joy, again return'd!
lines.plainText: Talbot my life my joy again return'd

lines.text: How wert thou handled, being prisoner?
lines.plainText: How wert thou handled being prisoner

lines.text: Or by what means got'st thou to be releas'd?
lines.plainText: Or by what means got'st thou to be releas'd

lines.text: Discourse, I prithee, on this turret's top.
lines.plainText: Discourse I prithee on this turret's top

lines.text: The Duke of Bedford had a prisoner
lines.plainText: The Duke of Bedford had a prisoner

lines.text: Call'd the brave Lord Ponton de Santrailles;
lines.plainText: Call'd the brave Lord Ponton de Santrailles

lines.text: For him was I exchanged and ransomed.
lines.plainText: For him was I exchanged and ransomed

lines.text: But with a baser man of arms by far
lines.plainText: But with a baser man of arms by far

lines.text: Once in contempt they would have barter'd me,
lines.plainText: Once in contempt they would have barter'd me

lines.text: Which I disdaining scorn'd, and craved death
lines.plainText: Which I disdaining scorn'd and craved death

lines.text: Rather than I would be so vile-esteem'd.
lines.plainText: Rather than I would be so vileesteem'd

lines.text: In fine, redeem'd I was as I desired.
lines.plainText: In fine redeem'd I was as I desired

lines.text: But O, the treacherous Fastolf wounds my heart,
lines.plainText: But O the treacherous Fastolf wounds my heart

lines.text: Whom with my bare fists I would execute
lines.plainText: Whom with my bare fists I would execute

lines.text: If I now had him brought into my power.
lines.plainText: If I now had him brought into my power

lines.text: Yet tell'st thou not how thou wert entertain'd.
lines.plainText: Yet tell'st thou not how thou wert entertain'd

lines.text: With scoffs and scorns and contumelious taunts.
lines.plainText: With scoffs and scorns and contumelious taunts

lines.text: In open market-place produced they me
lines.plainText: In open marketplace produced they me

lines.text: To be a public spectacle to all.
lines.plainText: To be a public spectacle to all

lines.text: Here, said they, is the terror of the French,
lines.plainText: Here said they is the terror of the French

lines.text: The scarecrow that affrights our children so.
lines.plainText: The scarecrow that affrights our children so

lines.text: Then broke I from the officers that led me,
lines.plainText: Then broke I from the officers that led me

lines.text: And with my nails digg'd stones out of the ground
lines.plainText: And with my nails digg'd stones out of the ground

lines.text: To hurl at the beholders of my shame.
lines.plainText: To hurl at the beholders of my shame

lines.text: My grisly countenance made others fly;
lines.plainText: My grisly countenance made others fly

lines.text: None durst come near for fear of sudden death.
lines.plainText: None durst come near for fear of sudden death

lines.text: In iron walls they deem'd me not secure;
lines.plainText: In iron walls they deem'd me not secure

lines.text: So great fear of my name 'mongst them were spread
lines.plainText: So great fear of my name 'mongst them were spread

lines.text: That they supposed I could rend bars of steel
lines.plainText: That they supposed I could rend bars of steel

lines.text: And spurn in pieces posts of adamant.
lines.plainText: And spurn in pieces posts of adamant

lines.text: Wherefore a guard of chosen shot I had,
lines.plainText: Wherefore a guard of chosen shot I had

lines.text: That walk'd about me every minute while;
lines.plainText: That walk'd about me every minute while

lines.text: And if I did but stir out of my bed,
lines.plainText: And if I did but stir out of my bed

lines.text: Ready they were to shoot me to the heart.
lines.plainText: Ready they were to shoot me to the heart

content.text: Enter the Boy with a linstock.

lines.text: I grieve to hear what torments you endured,
lines.plainText: I grieve to hear what torments you endured

lines.text: But we will be revenged sufficiently.
lines.plainText: But we will be revenged sufficiently

lines.text: Now it is supper-time in Orleans.
lines.plainText: Now it is suppertime in Orleans

lines.text: Here, through this grate, I count each one
lines.plainText: Here through this grate I count each one

lines.text: And view the Frenchmen how they fortify.
lines.plainText: And view the Frenchmen how they fortify

lines.text: Let us look in; the sight will much delight thee.
lines.plainText: Let us look in the sight will much delight thee

lines.text: Sir Thomas Gargrave and Sir William Glansdale,
lines.plainText: Sir Thomas Gargrave and Sir William Glansdale

lines.text: Let me have your express opinions
lines.plainText: Let me have your express opinions

lines.text: Where is best place to make our battery next.
lines.plainText: Where is best place to make our battery next

lines.text: I think, at the north gate, for there stand lords.
lines.plainText: I think at the north gate for there stand lords

lines.text: And I, here, at the bulwark of the bridge.
lines.plainText: And I here at the bulwark of the bridge

lines.text: For aught I see, this city must be famish'd,
lines.plainText: For aught I see this city must be famish'd

lines.text: Or with light skirmishes enfeebled.
lines.plainText: Or with light skirmishes enfeebled

content.text: Here they shoot, and Salisbury and Gargrave fall down.

lines.text: O Lord, have mercy on us, wretched sinners!
lines.plainText: O Lord have mercy on us wretched sinners

lines.text: O Lord, have mercy on me, woeful man!
lines.plainText: O Lord have mercy on me woeful man

lines.text: What chance is this that suddenly hath cross'd us?
lines.plainText: What chance is this that suddenly hath cross'd us

lines.text: Speak, Salisbury; at least, if thou canst speak!
lines.plainText: Speak Salisbury at least if thou canst speak

lines.text: How far'st thou, mirror of all martial men?
lines.plainText: How far'st thou mirror of all martial men

lines.text: One of thy eyes and thy cheek's side struck off!
lines.plainText: One of thy eyes and thy cheek's side struck off

lines.text: Accursed tower, accursed fatal hand
lines.plainText: Accursed tower accursed fatal hand

lines.text: That hath contrived this woeful tragedy!
lines.plainText: That hath contrived this woeful tragedy

lines.text: In thirteen battles Salisbury o'ercame;
lines.plainText: In thirteen battles Salisbury o'ercame

lines.text: Henry the Fifth he first train'd to the wars;
lines.plainText: Henry the Fifth he first train'd to the wars

lines.text: Whilst any trump did sound, or drum struck up,
lines.plainText: Whilst any trump did sound or drum struck up

lines.text: His sword did ne'er leave striking in the field.
lines.plainText: His sword did ne'er leave striking in the field

lines.text: Yet liv'st thou, Salisbury? Though thy speech doth fail,
lines.plainText: Yet liv'st thou Salisbury Though thy speech doth fail

lines.text: One eye thou hast to look to heaven for grace.
lines.plainText: One eye thou hast to look to heaven for grace

lines.text: The sun with one eye vieweth all the world.
lines.plainText: The sun with one eye vieweth all the world

lines.text: Heaven, be thou gracious to none alive,
lines.plainText: Heaven be thou gracious to none alive

lines.text: If Salisbury wants mercy at thy hands!
lines.plainText: If Salisbury wants mercy at thy hands

lines.text: Sir Thomas Gargrave, hast thou any life?
lines.plainText: Sir Thomas Gargrave hast thou any life

lines.text: Speak unto Talbot; nay, look up to him.
lines.plainText: Speak unto Talbot nay look up to him

lines.text: Bear hence his body; I will help to bury it.
lines.plainText: Bear hence his body I will help to bury it

content.text: [Exeunt some with the body of Gargrave.]
[Here an alarum, and it thunders and lightens.]

lines.text: My lord, my lord, the French have gather'd head.
lines.plainText: My lord my lord the French have gather'd head

lines.text: The Dauphin, with one Joan la Pucelle join'd,
lines.plainText: The Dauphin with one Joan la Pucelle join'd

lines.text: A holy prophetess new risen up,
lines.plainText: A holy prophetess new risen up

lines.text: Is come with a great power to raise the siege.
lines.plainText: Is come with a great power to raise the siege

content.text: [Here Salisbury lifteth himself up and groans.]

lines.text: Hear, hear how dying Salisbury doth groan;
lines.plainText: Hear hear how dying Salisbury doth groan

lines.text: It irks his heart he cannot be revenged.
lines.plainText: It irks his heart he cannot be revenged

lines.text: Frenchmen, I'll be a Salisbury to you.
lines.plainText: Frenchmen I'll be a Salisbury to you

lines.text: Pucelle or puzel, dolphin or dogfish,
lines.plainText: Pucelle or puzel dolphin or dogfish

lines.text: Your hearts I'll stamp out with my horse's heels
lines.plainText: Your hearts I'll stamp out with my horse's heels

lines.text: And make a quagmire of your mingled brains.
lines.plainText: And make a quagmire of your mingled brains

lines.text: Convey we Salisbury into his tent,
lines.plainText: Convey we Salisbury into his tent

lines.text: And then we'll try what these dastard Frenchmen dare.
lines.plainText: And then we'll try what these dastard Frenchmen dare
